description: The pie chart, titled “Stimulus Type,” visually represents the proportional distribution of different types of input materials journalists provided to large language models (LLMs) during WildChat conversations, as matched to online articles from two news agencies. The chart is divided into ten distinct, color-coded segments, each labeled with its category name and precise percentage. The largest segment, “Draft/Other,” occupies 26.4% of the chart and is colored in deep red. Following this are “Press Release” at 18.7% (golden yellow) and “External News Article” at 18.1% (dark green). “Interview” accounts for 8.8% (navy blue), while “Organizational Report” represents 7.7% (light purple) and “Event Posting” 6.6% (maroon). Smaller segments include “Organizational Website” and “Intra-agency news article,” both at 4.9% (lavender and sky blue, respectively), “Email” at 2.7% (light green), and “Social Media Post” at 1.1% (orange). Each slice is clearly labeled with its percentage, and the chart uses a donut-style layout with a central white space containing the title. Notably, the caption contains minor inaccuracies: it incorrectly states “Organizational Report” as 9.7% (it is 7.7%) and misreports “Social Media Post” as 1.5% (it is 1.1%), while also reversing the comparison with “Email” — in fact, “Email” (2.7%) is larger than “Social Media Post” (1.1%). The chart effectively conveys the relative frequency of stimulus types, with no segments exploded or emphasized beyond their proportional size.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of various input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs during WildChat conversations, matched to online articles from two identified news agencies. The largest category is 'Draft/Other,' accounting for approximately 26.4% of the total, followed by 'Press Release' at 18.7%. 'External News Article' and 'Interview' are the next largest categories, representing 18.1% and 8.8%, respectively. Notably, 'Organizational Report' consistently exceeds 'Event Posting,' with 9.7% compared to 6.6%. Additionally, 'Social Media Post' shows a slight increase over 'Email,' with 1.5% versus 2.7%. The chart provides a clear overview of the relative proportions of each stimulus type, with all categories labeled and color-coded for clarity.
